title: Naan-e barbari
subtitle: Persian flatbread with sesame and nigella seeds
excerpt: Naan-e barbari is a long, ridged Persian flatbread with a golden, slightly chewy crust and a fluffy interior. Brushed with a simple starch glaze and scattered with sesame and nigella seeds before baking, it is one of the most widely eaten breads in Iran and a natural companion to most Persian dishes.
sourceNotes: One of five main types of Iranian flatbread. Barbari is the thickest and most widely sold at breakfast time. The name refers to the Barbar people of eastern Iran.

recipe.freezeNotes: Baked barbari freezes well. Wrap in foil and reheat in a 180 C oven for 8 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made the evening before and refrigerated overnight for a slow cold rise. Shape and bake the next day.
recipe.temperatureNote: Very hot oven — preheat fully for at least 30 minutes

content.text: Naan-e barbari is the bread most Iranians eat at breakfast: long and oval, about 30 to 40 cm, with a ridged surface and a shiny golden crust from the starch glaze. The inside is soft and slightly chewy, not dry like many flatbreads.

The glaze is the detail that makes barbari distinct. A simple mixture of flour, water, oil, and a pinch of baking soda is brushed over the shaped dough before baking. It creates a burnished, slightly lacquered finish that ordinary breads lack.
The bread must be baked at a very high temperature. Preheat the oven for at least 30 minutes before baking and use the hottest shelf.

Mix the flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in a large bowl. Add the oil and warm water. Bring together into a dough and knead for 8 to 10 minutes by hand, or 6 minutes in a stand mixer with a dough hook, until smooth and elastic. Shape into a ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and leave to rise for 60 to 90 minutes until doubled.

Divide the dough into two pieces. On a lightly floured surface, shape each into an oval about 30 cm long and 15 cm wide. Place on a lightly oiled baking sheet. Leave to rest for 20 minutes while you preheat the oven to 240 C.

Whisk together the glaze ingredients (flour, water, oil, bicarbonate) until smooth. Brush generously over the surface of each bread. Use your fingertips to press five or six parallel grooves lengthways into each loaf, going about halfway through the dough. Scatter the sesame and nigella seeds into the grooves and over the surface. Bake at 240 C for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped on the base. Eat the same day.

rows.cause: Oven not hot enough or glaze too thin
rows.fix: Preheat fully for 30 minutes. Apply glaze generously; a thin layer does not give the signature finish.

rows.cause: Slightly high hydration, which is normal
rows.fix: Flour your hands well and work quickly. The dough is meant to be soft.

rows.cause: Grooves not deep enough or dough over-proved
rows.fix: Press firmly with floured fingers; the grooves should be clearly visible. Bake promptly after shaping.

content.text: Poppy seeds can replace or supplement the nigella. For a slightly richer bread, replace 2 tbsp of water with whole milk. A stone or heavy baking steel in the oven gives an even better base crust.
The dough can be refrigerated overnight after its first rise. Shape and bake the next day. Baked bread is best eaten the same day; freeze any leftovers as soon as they have cooled.

Barbari is the most popular bread in Iran and the one most likely to be found at a Persian breakfast table alongside fresh herbs, feta, butter, and honey. It is sold in dedicated bread shops (noonvai) that bake it fresh throughout the morning. In the UK it can be found in Iranian grocery shops.
